title: Metacult
targetDuration: 1–2 minutes; hard maximum 120 seconds after measured voice timing

scenes.title: Belonging without surrender
scenes.viewerPurpose: Good intentions alone may fail to sustain a group. A proposed voluntary, nonexclusive cultural institution combines collective capacity with explicit limits on leaders and a protected right of exit.
scenes.composition: Two people tend a shared hearth while separate small efforts remain visible nearby. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Two people tend a shared hearth while separate small efforts remain visible nearby.
Hold both people as a path away from the hearth stays open.

cues.text: Why do good causes so often lack the staying power of groups we distrust?
cues.visualAction: Two people tend a shared hearth while separate small efforts remain visible nearby.
cues.emotion: Sincere curiosity; gently emphasize “staying power”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: Metacult proposes communities that can act together while protecting each member’s right to doubt, disagree, and leave.
cues.visualAction: Hold both people as a path away from the hearth stays open.
cues.emotion: Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “right to doubt”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.

scenes.title: What holds a cause together
scenes.viewerPurpose: Isolation has a cost for worthwhile convictions. Effective belonging can threaten personal independence.

cues.text: Stories and commitment create strength, but leaders can also hide decisions, punish doubt, and exploit loyalty.
cues.visualAction: A treasurer pauses with funds beside a record another member can inspect.

cues.text: Its proposed community protects doubt, other loyalties, and the freedom to leave.
